theme: The Olivet Discourse; virgins, talents, sheep and goats
readingInstruction: Read Matthew 24:1-25:46. This is the Olivet Discourse, followed by three parables: the ten virgins, the talents, and the sheep and goats. It is a long reading, so take it in three parts. Notice the repeated call to watch and be ready.
settingTheScene: As Jesus leaves the temple, the disciples point out its buildings. He says that not one stone will be left on another. Later, on the Mount of Olives, they ask when this will happen and what will be the sign of his coming and the close of the age. Jesus’ answer includes the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70, and it also looks further to his return. The point of the chapters is not to give a timetable but to call for readiness.
observation: “See that no one leads you astray. For many will come in my name, saying, I am the Christ” (24:4-5).
“But the one who endures to the end will be saved” (24:13).
“And this gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come” (24:14).
“Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away” (24:35).
“But concerning that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son, but the Father only” (24:36).
“Watch therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming” (24:42).
“Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much” (25:21).
“Truly, I say to you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me” (25:40).
interpretation:
The discourse mixes near and far. Jesus warns of false messiahs, wars, famines, persecution, and the abomination of desolation, details that were fulfilled in part in the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70. He also speaks of his coming “like lightning” and the gathering of his elect. Scholars differ on how to divide the near and far. What is clear is the pattern: before the end there will be trouble, the gospel will go to all nations, and no one will know the day.

The repeated call is to be ready. The faithful servant is the one found working when the master returns. This is not paranoia but steady faithfulness.

Three parables apply the point. The ten virgins: five were wise and took extra oil, and five were foolish. When the bridegroom came at midnight, the foolish ones were shut out. Readiness cannot be borrowed at the last minute. The talents: a master entrusts money to three servants and goes away. Two invest and double it, and the third buries his out of fear. The master praises faithfulness and condemns the one who did nothing. We are to use what Jesus has entrusted to us.

The sheep and goats is the final scene of judgment. The Son of Man sits on his throne and separates the nations. The sheep are those who fed the hungry, welcomed the stranger, clothed the naked, and visited the sick and imprisoned, and they did so to Jesus without knowing it. The goats failed to do so. The standard is not a list of achievements but the fruit of a changed heart: love shown to the least of these, who are Christ’s brothers.

The discourse ends on a note of both warning and hope. The King will return. Those who are his will be welcomed into the kingdom prepared for them since the foundation of the world.
connection: Daniel 7:13-14 and 9:27 stand behind the language of the Son of Man and the abomination. 1 Thessalonians 4:13-5:11 describes the Lord’s return and the call to be awake. 2 Peter 3:8-13 explains the delay. Luke 19:11-27 gives a similar parable of the minas. James 2:14-17 says faith without works is dead. Revelation 20:11-15 depicts the final judgment. Titus 2:13 speaks of waiting for the blessed hope.
application:
Ask what you have been entrusted with, such as time, gifts, resources, and relationships. How can you invest it for the King?

Do one concrete act of mercy for “the least of these” this week.

Live ready, not fearful: do today’s work faithfully, knowing that he is coming.
prayerPrompts: Tell Jesus you are watching and ready, or ask him to make you so.
Ask him for the faithfulness that lasts like oil in a lamp.
Ask him to show you how to care for the least of these.
